followup: PLAN (s) S6; frozen (q)/(r) programs, not re-scored

overlap.description: Fires when the opponent threatens an immediate win in the leftmost column (a must-block landing cell in column 0), most strongly for a vertical three of their stones in column 0, weaker for a horizontal three, and barely for diagonal ones; weakened when there are other threats or late in the game. Weak firing also occurs diffusely in early openings and some must-blocks in column 5 without a clear rule.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked on top of the rightmost column (column 6) with the cell above still empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 6; strongest when the threat cell is low (row 3) and weaker for a top-row threat. The same vertical three in any other column barely fires it. A diffuse weak tail (about 70% of firing, low activation) has no single rule; it is enriched for opponent two-stacks on column 6.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 0 (leftmost) with the cell above empty: a vertical must-block in column 0. Weaker if I also have an immediate win; my own vertical three in column 0 fires weakly. Horizontal or diagonal threats at column 0, and vertical threes in other columns, do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stacked on top of column 0 with the cell above empty (I must block in column 0), whether or not they just played there; also on other opponent must-blocks in column 0 (e.g. diagonal, weaker; horizontal row-0 threats do not count). Weaker firing when the opponent just dropped the third stone into column 0 mid/late game. Not my own column-0 three, nor stacks in other columns.

Fires when the opponent has an immediate win in column 6 (the rightmost column) that I must block, above the bottom row; strongest (20-40) when their last move just made it, typically a vertical three in column 6 or a horizontal three ending at column 6. Weak firing (1-4) for freshly made vertical threes in other columns (0,1,4,5). Bottom-row threats at (0,6) and stale threats barely fire.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 1 (second column from the left) with the cell above empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 1; very strong (20-65), especially right after they played there. A vertical three in column 5 gives weak firing (about 1-2). Horizontal/diagonal threats in column 1, my own vertical threes, and other columns do not fire it. Much weak near-threshold firing is unexplained.

Late-game signal that column 5 (second from the right) is full. It almost never fires unless column 5 is full. Given that, it gets stronger when few columns are left (strongest with one or two playable columns), when an open column is nearly empty, and when the player to move is losing by force. It is weak when column 5 still has room, even in a lost endgame.

Fires when the opponent has a vertical run on top of column 0 (the leftmost column) with the cell above still empty: strongly (act 4-20) for an open vertical three in column 0 (a must-block), weakly (about 1-3) for an opponent pair at rows 2-3 of column 0 with column 0 exactly four high. The same threats in other columns, my own stones, and pairs at other heights do not make it fire.

Fires when the opponent is building the bottom-left diagonal (0,0)-(1,1)-(2,2)-(3,3) (a1-d4): they hold at least 3 of those 4 cells and I hold none, i.e. they threaten the 4th cell; also when they hold (1,1),(3,3),(4,4) with (2,2) empty. Opponent holding only (0,0)+(1,1) gives weak, inconsistent activation. Own stones on that diagonal, the mirror diagonal, or shifted diagonals do not make it fire.

Fires when the opponent threatens to win in column 6 (rightmost), mainly when they have three stones stacked vertically on top of column 6 with the cell above empty (strongest for a stack at rows 0-2). A non-vertical must-block in column 6 above the bottom row fires weakly. Does not fire for a bottom-row horizontal threat at column 6, stacks in other columns, or my own column-6 stack (strongly negative).

Fires when the leftmost column (column 0) is exactly three stones high with an opponent stone on top, so the next stone there lands in row 4. Strongest (often 5-9) when the opponent has just played there to make three in a row up column 0 (a must-block); mixed stacks like mine-mine-theirs fire weakly and only about half the time. Vertical threes in other columns, or column 0 at other heights, do not fire.

Weak partial pattern: early game (ply <= 18), I moved first, no immediate win, and the bottom two rows of columns 2-3 form a checkerboard: column 2 empty or my stone capped by theirs, column 3 empty or their stone with mine on top. Odd column-2 heights, column-3 height 1, or the opposite colours switch it off. Other stones modulate it unpredictably.

units_with_tactic_agreement_ge_0.5.description: Fires when the opponent threatens an immediate win in the leftmost column (a must-block landing cell in column 0), most strongly for a vertical three of their stones in column 0, weaker for a horizontal three, and barely for diagonal ones; weakened when there are other threats or late in the game. Weak firing also occurs diffusely in early openings and some must-blocks in column 5 without a clear rule.

Fires when the opponent threatens to win in column 6 (rightmost), mainly when they have three stones stacked vertically on top of column 6 with the cell above empty (strongest for a stack at rows 0-2). A non-vertical must-block in column 6 above the bottom row fires weakly. Does not fire for a bottom-row horizontal threat at column 6, stacks in other columns, or my own column-6 stack (strongly negative).

No clean concept found; firing is diffuse. Weak tendency: fires when I must block an immediate opponent threat, strongest (top 0.1%) when the opponent just played column 3 and now threatens to win on the top cell of column 3 via a row or diagonal. Plain vertical threats in column 3, and bottom-row threats, do not fire. Many firings have no threat at all, often with column 3 full.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked on top of the rightmost column (column 6) with the cell above still empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 6; strongest when the threat cell is low (row 3) and weaker for a top-row threat. The same vertical three in any other column barely fires it. A diffuse weak tail (about 70% of firing, low activation) has no single rule; it is enriched for opponent two-stacks on column 6.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stacked on top of column 0 with the cell above empty (I must block in column 0), whether or not they just played there; also on other opponent must-blocks in column 0 (e.g. diagonal, weaker; horizontal row-0 threats do not count). Weaker firing when the opponent just dropped the third stone into column 0 mid/late game. Not my own column-0 three, nor stacks in other columns.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 0 (leftmost) with the cell above empty, so I must block there; strongest early in the game, weaker late. The same three in another column, horizontal or diagonal threats at column 0, my own three there, or an already-blocked three do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 0 (leftmost) with the cell above empty: a vertical must-block in column 0. Weaker if I also have an immediate win; my own vertical three in column 0 fires weakly. Horizontal or diagonal threats at column 0, and vertical threes in other columns, do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.

No clean concept found. Weakly more likely to fire when there is an immediate win or must-block cell in column 4, or when columns 2-3 stand at least two stones taller than columns 1 and 4 with same-colour horizontal pairs across columns 2-3. Most firing is not explained by these; activation is highly conjunctive and depends on move order.

Fires when the opponent has a vertical run on top of column 0 (the leftmost column) with the cell above still empty: strongly (act 4-20) for an open vertical three in column 0 (a must-block), weakly (about 1-3) for an opponent pair at rows 2-3 of column 0 with column 0 exactly four high. The same threats in other columns, my own stones, and pairs at other heights do not make it fire.

Fires when the opponent has an immediate win in column 6 (the rightmost column) that I must block, above the bottom row; strongest (20-40) when their last move just made it, typically a vertical three in column 6 or a horizontal three ending at column 6. Weak firing (1-4) for freshly made vertical threes in other columns (0,1,4,5). Bottom-row threats at (0,6) and stale threats barely fire.

all.description: Fires when the center column (3) holds exactly four stones and the top one (row 4 from the bottom) is the opponent's, so my next center drop lands on the fifth row. It is strongest when the opponent also owns the stone(s) just below (a vertical two or three ending at that cell) and when they just played it, and in earlier positions; weak late in the game. Never fires for other columns or other center heights.

No clean concept. Fires mostly in the opening (ply 3-16) while the centre column is empty or has one stone, more so when my bottom-row stones sit on columns 1-2 and/or 4-5 (e.g. .XX..OO) and the opponent holds the bottom-right corner; my stone in a bottom corner or their stone on (0,1)/(0,5) suppresses it. Very sensitive to single stones and not mirror-symmetric.

Fires when column 6 (rightmost) is full and its top cell holds an opponent stone, strongest right after the opponent has just topped off column 6. It is boosted when column 2 is still low (3 or fewer stones) and columns 4 and 5 are (nearly) full, and weaker if the cell below the top is mine. If my stone tops column 6 it is near zero, except weak firing when the cell below is theirs.

Fires when exactly one stone is on the board: the opponent has made the first move and I am about to make my first. Strongest if that stone is in column 5, then column 0, then 4; columns 1-3 barely fire, column 6 does not. A few later positions also just cross the threshold, mostly right after the opponent plays column 0 or on the 41st move, with no clean rule.

Fires when the opponent threatens an immediate win in the leftmost column (a must-block landing cell in column 0), most strongly for a vertical three of their stones in column 0, weaker for a horizontal three, and barely for diagonal ones; weakened when there are other threats or late in the game. Weak firing also occurs diffusely in early openings and some must-blocks in column 5 without a clear rule.

Fires when the opponent owns the lower-centre staircase: their stones on the bottom of column 3, the second row of columns 3 and 4, and the third row of column 5 (the diagonal (0,3)-(1,4)-(2,5) pointing at (3,6)), usually with my stone on top of column 4 at row 2 and cell (1,2) not theirs. Stronger at odd ply (I am second player) and later in the game. The same stones owned by me do not fire it.

Fires late in the game right after the opponent plays column 5 while column 5 is still short (usually 2-4 stones) and several other columns are full. Strongest after two or three consecutive column-5 moves, and when the first player moved last. Weak if the last move was elsewhere, early in the game, or column 5 is nearly full. It also depends on move order, not just the board.

No clean concept. Fires most when the opponent has built a cluster in the lower-left/center, especially stones on (2,2), (1,3), (1,2), (2,1), (3,1), often with the last opponent stone just placed at (2,1)/(2,2)/(3,1), column 4 empty, and none of my stones on (0,4), (1,3) or (2,2). Such positions are often forced or lost for me, but threats alone do not predict firing.

Fires mostly when the board is left-heavy with column 2 empty (or one stone) between tall columns 1 and 3 (column 3 four or more high, column 0 also filled) and columns 4-6 short; also always right after an opening move in column 0. Strength depends strongly on who owns the lower stones (adding one far stone to flip the side to move often switches it off), so many such wells do not fire.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked on top of the rightmost column (column 6) with the cell above still empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 6; strongest when the threat cell is low (row 3) and weaker for a top-row threat. The same vertical three in any other column barely fires it. A diffuse weak tail (about 70% of firing, low activation) has no single rule; it is enriched for opponent two-stacks on column 6.

No clean concept found. Weakly: fires when the opponent holds cells (2,4)/(3,3)/(2,5) and I hold the bottom of column 2, and almost never when I hold (3,3) or (2,4) or the opponent holds (0,2) or (3,4). Strongest case: opponent stones at (0,4),(1,4),(1,5) over my (0,5) with my stones at (0,2),(0,3). In 3-stone openings it fires when the opponent has the corner (0,0) uncovered. Shifted or mirrored shapes do not fire.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 0 (leftmost) with the cell above empty: a vertical must-block in column 0. Weaker if I also have an immediate win; my own vertical three in column 0 fires weakly. Horizontal or diagonal threats at column 0, and vertical threes in other columns, do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.

No clean concept found. The strongest firing often occurs mid-game when column 4 is exactly four high with my stone on top at row 3 (landing cell (4,4) still empty), frequently with my stones stacked or paired at the centre on row 3 and the opponent's row-1 stones beneath; the opponent covering column 4 switches it off. But this covers only a small part of firing, and many early openings also fire irregularly.

Clearest at its strongest: early game, I am the first player (even ply), the opponent's stones sit on the bottom corners (0,0) and/or (0,6) (also (0,1)), and my stones hold the bottom center, with column 3 free of opponent stones (an opponent stone at (1,3) or on my center stone turns it off). Most threshold-level firing is in the middle game and fits no simple board rule; treat this as a partial, low-confidence description.

Fires right after the opponent drops a stone in column 0 (the left edge) that lands on row 3 or 4, i.e. the 4th or 5th stone in that column; 5th stone fires strongest. Tall columns 1 and 2 weaken it, and a 4th-stone drop late in the game usually does not fire. Other columns (including column 6), lower stones, the 6th stone, or a column-0 stack built a few moves earlier mostly do not fire.

Mostly an opening detector. It fires most strongly at ply 3 (second player to move) when the opponent's two stones are in the centre (cols 3-5, including col 4) and my stone is in col 4 or the opponent holds col 4 too, and less often at ply 5. A stone of mine in col 1 switches it off. About 70% of firing is scattered, near-threshold mid/late-game positions with no pattern I could find.

Fires mostly in the opening, on a fixed bottom-centre-right pattern: my stones at (0,4) and/or (0,5) hemmed in by opponent stones, especially an opponent stone directly on top of my column-5 bottom stone, and opponent stones at (0,2)/(0,3)/(1,2)/(1,3) to the left of my (0,4). My own stones at (0,6), (0,1) or in rows 1-2 of columns 2-5 suppress it. Not translation- or mirror-invariant. Weaker late-game firing is diffuse and not captured.

No clean concept found. It fires mostly in the opening and middlegame (ply 5-24) just after the opponent drops a stone in columns 1-4, often right on top of one of my stones or next to my low horizontal pairs, and never when I have an immediate win. These cues are weak (dev F1 0.06). Exact firing depends on very specific stone layouts, so it looks like a mixture or random direction.

Fires most strongly when I (to move) have three of a horizontal four on row 2 (third row) with the gap in column 1 or 2 still low (height 0-1), and opponent stones sit directly on top of my row-2 stones on row 3. Not for the same shape on other rows, the right side, or colors swapped; opponent stones low in column 4 suppress it. Many weak firings have no clear pattern.

No clean concept found. About a quarter of firing is at ply 3 (second player to move after three stones), for a specific, left-right asymmetric set of openings, mostly with an opponent stone in the bottom-left corner, on column 2's bottom cell, or stacked in column 5 (e.g. 5,5,5; 2,1,0; 0,1,2). The rest is scattered over midgame positions with no reliable cue; it never fires at ply 0-2.

Fires when column 4 holds a short stack (2-4 stones) containing opponent stones, ideally two or three of theirs, and the opponent played into column 4 within their last two moves. Empty columns 3 and 5 help; stones there, a tall or full column 4, later game, or several moves since the last column-4 move switch it off. Also briefly off right after an opponent stone lands on row 3+ of column 4 or on top of my stone.

Mostly an early-opening pattern with me (first player) to move: I hold the bottom of column 2 (often an X-O-X stack there), the opponent holds the bottom of the centre columns 3/4 (strongest just after they play there), I have no stone low in columns 3-4, and columns 0-1 are empty. If I took the centre bottom it does not fire; right-side mirror images do not fire. About half of firing is mid-game and unexplained.

Fires when the leftmost column (column 0) is full or nearly full (4-6 stones, strongest at 6), especially when most of those stones belong to the player to move, the last move was into column 0, column 1 is short, and the game is still fairly short (under ~26 stones). Long games, opponent-dominated column 0, or many stones in column 1 suppress it. Other columns being tall does not trigger it.

Fires strongly when the opponent has three stacked on top of column 0 with the cell above empty (I must block in column 0), whether or not they just played there; also on other opponent must-blocks in column 0 (e.g. diagonal, weaker; horizontal row-0 threats do not count). Weaker firing when the opponent just dropped the third stone into column 0 mid/late game. Not my own column-0 three, nor stacks in other columns.

Fires only right after the opponent drops a stone into the centre column (3) on top of at least one of MY stones there (never when it lands on the bottom row or on only their own stones), once the game is past roughly 12-14 stones. Stronger with 2-3 of my stones under it and more stones elsewhere; stones in column 4 (and 2, 5) weaken it.

Fires when column 1 (second from the left) holds exactly one stone, so the next stone there would land on row 1, and the board is fairly full: mostly from move ~15 on, more so with full columns (especially 0, 2, 3), a tall center column, and when the last move was that first stone in column 1. Doesn't fire if column 1 is empty or has 2+ stones. Early-game cases rarely fire.

Fires mainly when the opponent caps my vertical stack in column 5: their stone on row 4 directly above my stones, strongest when I own the three cells below. Same cap in column 3 is weaker. Suppressed when either side has threat cells, by opponent stones in column 2, and on crowded boards (ply above ~20). Also fires weakly in some early openings where the opponent stacks on my stone.

Fires on a fixed checkerboard of colours on the lower left-centre, seen from the player to move: column 2 has their stone at row 1 with mine on top, column 4 has mine at row 1 with theirs on top, and column 5 has theirs at the bottom with mine above. Columns 0-1 stay at most one stone high and column 3 stays low. Swapping colours or stacking columns 0-1 turns it off. Partial matches fire more weakly.

Early-to-mid game (ply up to ~14) right-side pattern: column 5 is empty, column 6 holds only opponent stones (strongest when they have stacked three there, a vertical must-block at (3,6)), and I hold the bottom of the centre column (3), often also (0,2)/(1,3), with an opponent stone at (1,2). My stones in column 6, opponent stones in column 5 or on (0,0),(0,1),(0,4) suppress it. Much weaker firing elsewhere is diffuse.

Fires when column 5 is empty and dropping a stone there would be bad for me because of the cell above, (1,5): the opponent already threatens a win at (1,5), would get new winning cells by playing there, or has 2-3 stones in open lines through (0,5)/(1,5). Off if col 5 has a stone, or (without a (1,5) threat) the opponent threatens (2,5) or any immediate win/must-block exists.

Weak, mixed layer-0 unit keyed to move order rather than tactics. It fires (1) when the opponent's last move was in the centre column 3 at ply 4 or 5, (2) right after an opening move in column 1, and (3) late in the game (ply 20+) when it is the first player's turn and the edge columns 0 and 6 hold many stones (about 9+), unless the last move was in column 0. Odd late plies are strongly negative.

Fires when column 2 is exactly two stones high with an opponent stone on top (row 1 of column 2 theirs, row 2 empty), strongest right after the opponent played it. My stones beside that empty cell (rows 1-3 of columns 1 and 3) raise it; opponent stones there, especially row 2 column 3, suppress it. Weak in the first few plies.

Fires in the opening (roughly ply <= 12) when I (the player to move) own the bottom-right corner (row 0, col 6) with no opponent stone stacked above it, and the opponent has stones on the bottom two rows in columns 0, 1, 3, 4 or 5. Stronger with more such opponent stones and fewer moves played; opponent stones in column 2 and my own stones in columns 4-5 weaken it. Without my corner stone it essentially never fires.

Weak, graded unit; no clean concept. Fires mostly in the early middlegame (about 8-15 stones) when the stones sit in a tall centre-left block: column 3 at height 4-5 (or empty) with column 2 built up to 3+, while columns 1, 4, 5, 6 stay nearly empty. Column 3 at height 1-3 or full, or stones piling up on the right, switch it off.

Two unrelated patterns. (1) Ply-3 openings with me second: my stone is not in column 3 or 5 and column 5 is empty (e.g. 3,2,4); strongest firing. (2) Crowded middlegames where the opponent holds row 4 of column 5 (0-indexed) and I hold row 4 of column 4, usually with their stone above or mine below in column 5. Many firings fit neither; possibly a distributed or random direction.

Fires right after the opponent drops a stone into column 2 (third column from the left), mainly when that stone lands on top of my own stones there: the more of my stones in column 2, the stronger; the opponent's own earlier column-2 stones weaken it. It is strongly timing-dependent: weak in the first ~12 moves, strongest around moves 16-22, fading slowly later. Moves in any other column never fire it.

Fires when the right edge column (column 6) holds exactly 3 stones, so the next stone there lands in the 4th row, and the board is well filled elsewhere: at least three of columns 0-5 have 4+ stones (full central columns 3-4 matter most). It is weak or negative in the opening and is often damped right after a stone was just dropped into column 6.

No clean concept found. Weakly more likely to fire when there is an immediate win or must-block cell in column 4, or when columns 2-3 stand at least two stones taller than columns 1 and 4 with same-colour horizontal pairs across columns 2-3. Most firing is not explained by these; activation is highly conjunctive and depends on move order.

Loosely: fires in the middlegame (about 6-22 stones) when column 2 is completely empty while the centre (columns 3-5) holds stones, typically with my stone at the bottom of column 3 and column 1 also empty or low. Any stone in column 2 nearly always switches it off. Short openings and positions with many opponent stones in column 4 do not fire. This is only a partial, weak description (F1 ~0.3).

Fires when column 2 is stacked tall (about 4-6 stones, either colour) while the rest of the board is still sparse: early-to-middle game boards where many moves went into column 2. Opponent stones in columns 0, 1 and 3 suppress it most; more stones anywhere dilute it. A lone first move in column 2 also fires. A tall column 2 late in a crowded game usually does not fire.

Fires when column 1 (second from left) holds exactly three stones, so the next stone there lands on row 3 (fourth row), unless some other column has an immediate win or must-block. Strongest when the opponent just made column 1 three high and/or (3,1) is itself an immediate win or must-block; weak in the first ~10 plies. Never fires when column 1 has 0-2 or 4+ stones.

No clean concept found. The strongest firing is in mid or late games right after the opponent drops a stone in column 1 (rows 3-4 counting from 1) or at row 4 of column 4, leaving me one sensible reply, usually in column 1 or 4, often directly on top of that stone. Most firing positions do not fit this, and simple early forced blocks in those columns do not fire.

Fires only in the opening (about the first 2-7 plies, mostly when I moved first and the opponent has just replied), when the opponent's latest stone is in column 0, 3, 5 or 6 and no stones are in column 1. Opponent stones in columns 1 or 2 switch it off, as does any stone of mine in column 1. Stacks of three in columns 0 or 5 drive it highest. It is silent in midgames.

Mainly an opening detector: fires right after the game's first stone when the opponent played it in column 6, 0, 1 or 3 (strongest for 6). Columns 2, 4 and 5 do not fire it. The other ~44% of firing is in mid-to-late boards with no clear tactical pattern. There the activation builds up over plies after one side's moves and is only weakly tied to last moves in column 6 or the top row.

Fires when column 2 holds exactly two stones (next stone there would land on row 2), mainly in the opening (up to about move 7) or the late game (move 28+, most columns full). In the middlegame it fires mostly only when column 2 is my stone with the opponent's stone on top. Column 2 with 3 stones fires only very late; 1 or 4+ stones never.

Mid-game (about 8-23 stones) positions where column 2 is either untouched or completely full, columns 0 and 4 are nearly empty (or col 4 full), column 5 is 2-4 high and column 6 is 2-3 high with my stone at its bottom and the opponent's stone on top. A partly filled column 2, especially with an opponent stone in it, switches it off. Near threshold it is diffuse; no single rule covers most firing.

Fires when the opponent has an immediate win in column 6 (the rightmost column) that I must block, above the bottom row; strongest (20-40) when their last move just made it, typically a vertical three in column 6 or a horizontal three ending at column 6. Weak firing (1-4) for freshly made vertical threes in other columns (0,1,4,5). Bottom-row threats at (0,6) and stale threats barely fire.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 1 (second column from the left) with the cell above empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 1; very strong (20-65), especially right after they played there. A vertical three in column 5 gives weak firing (about 1-2). Horizontal/diagonal threats in column 1, my own vertical threes, and other columns do not fire it. Much weak near-threshold firing is unexplained.

No clean concept found. Activation is a board-state function seen from the player to move, mostly mid-game, loosely tied to stones in the lower centre-right and column 0: opponent stones at (1,0),(2,0) and (0,3), mine at (1,3) and (2,4), opponent at (1,4). These cells raise it on average, but stones elsewhere can switch it on or off, so no simple rule predicts firing well.

Fires mainly at the very start of the game: the opponent has played exactly one stone, in any column except the two edge columns (strongest for column 4, then 3). Single edge stones (columns 0 or 6) stay just below threshold. About a quarter of firing (including the strongest cases, e.g. after 6,6,4) happens in quiet early positions, often right after an opponent move in column 4. That part has no simple board rule.

Fires only late in the game when the board is nearly full: from about 34 stones when the player to move moved first (even stone count), and only from about 39 stones otherwise. Stronger when the last move was in column 6 (or 0), weaker after a move in columns 2-4, and weaker when columns 3, 4 or 6 still have open space; an open column 2 (or 0/1) helps. Never fires before ~30 stones, regardless of tactics.

Opening/early-middlegame pattern detector (ply <= ~15) built from specific bottom cells: fires when I have a stone at the bottom of column 2 and the opponent holds the bottom of columns 1 and 5, or holds a column-3 stack (their stones at rows 1 and 3 of column 3 around mine). Also fires on the 1-ply opening in column 1. An opponent stone at the bottom of column 6, or mine at the bottom of column 5, suppresses it.

Fires right after the opponent, who moved first (odd ply), drops a stone in column 5 or 4; strongest on the very first move of the game (opening in col 5 is the maximum, col 4 next). In later positions it fires only if the history is favourable: opponent stones in columns 3-5 raise it, while my stones in columns 0, 1 or 4 and opponent stones in column 0 suppress it. Never fires when I moved first.

Fires most strongly right after the very first move of the game when the opponent opened on the right edge (column 6, strongest) or column 5, and weakly for a column-0 opening; centre/other openings stay just below threshold. The remaining firing (about half) is scattered over mid- and late-game positions near threshold with no clean board pattern (slightly more when the last move was in column 0, 3 or 6).

No clean concept found. Fires mostly on sparse, early-to-middle boards where columns 0-1 on the left are still empty (especially column 1), the opponent has low stones in the centre or right (bottom of column 3, columns 5-6, sometimes stacked), and my own stones are not in the low centre. It is strongly left/right asymmetric (mirrored positions do not fire), and it is low when stones sit in column 1 or when I stack on the centre.

No clean concept; a diffuse board template. Fires mostly in early/middle games where the opponent just played on an edge or even column (6 or 0, sometimes 2; rarely 1/3/5), column 4 holds only 1-2 stones (a third stone there shuts it off), columns 1, 3 and 5 are empty or low, and the opponent owns the bottom of columns 0 and 4 and/or a vertical stack on top of column 6.

Fires mostly when column 1 (second from left) is completely empty, the bottom of column 2 is empty or mine (not the opponent's), and the opponent has stones stacked in the centre (column 3/4), often with a second empty column further right. An opponent stone at the bottom of column 1 or 2 switches it off. Weaker firing in the threshold band is mixed (late-game deep empty wells) and not captured well.

Strongest when the opponent has three stones stacked on top of column 0 (also column 2, sometimes 4) with the cell above empty, so I must block there; stronger when I have stones in the centre (cols 3-4) of the bottom row. Same threats in columns 1, 3, 5, 6, and horizontal threats, do not fire. Most weaker firing (near threshold) is in quiet positions with no clear pattern.

Late endgame (about ply 26+) where play is confined to at most three open columns, typically one nearly empty column (most strongly the center) with the rest of the board full, and the player to move is lost by force, usually because the opponent's threat cells in that column fall on the opponent's turn. Fires on alternate plies (the losing side's turns). Lost positions with 4+ open columns do not fire; some 1-2-column endgames fire even when not lost.

Fires when the center column (column 3) holds exactly three stones and the top one (row 3 from the bottom) is the opponent's, strongest right after the opponent has just played it there, especially early in the game. It fades within a few plies if other moves follow, and is off when column 3 has 2 or 4+ stones or the top center stone is mine. Other columns do nothing.

No clean concept found. It is strongest in sparse, early positions where I own the bottom-left corner (0,0) while the opponent holds bottom-row stones at the right edge (col 6) and in cols 1/2 (often stacked), and their stone sits on mine at (2,4); an opponent stone at bottom centre (0,3) suppresses it. It is side-to-move specific and left/right asymmetric. It fades as the centre fills, and many firings fit no simple rule.

Strongest when the opponent has just dropped a stone low into the centre column (column 3) and column 3 holds only their stones: the first stone in an empty centre column after 9+ moves, or a second on their own first after 13+ moves. Grows with move count and stones in columns 2 and 4. Not if my stone is in column 3 or the drop lands row 2+. Most weak firing is diffuse and uncovered.

Fires mainly when column 5 holds exactly one stone (cell above it empty) and the opponent has stones around it on the bottom two rows of columns 3-5: typically opponent stones at the bottom of columns 3 and 5 and/or on row 2 of columns 3-4, with my stone at the bottom of column 4 or 6. My stone on row 2 of column 3, or any stone at row 2 of column 5, largely switches it off.

Fires only when column 4 holds exactly two stones, so the next stone there lands at row 3 (cell (2,4)). Among those positions it fires mainly when the columns on either side (3 and 5) are stacked up beside that empty cell, and most strongly right after the opponent has played the second stone in column 4. The colours of the nearby stones matter (who is to move), but I found no simple rule for that.

Fires mainly when the opponent's last move is in column 3 (or 2, sometimes 1), the opponent has stones in column 2, I own stones in columns 5/6, and there are few opponent stones in column 3 or of mine in columns 0/4. Each stone adds only a little, so there is no sharp pattern. In very short games a reversed pattern also fires: I hold column 0 and they hold columns 3/4.

Fires when column 0 (the leftmost column) is completely full, most strongly on the move right after the opponent drops the stone that fills it. The signal fades over the following moves, slowly if column 0 filled early in the game and fast if it filled late. It is weak when column 0 fills on a nearly full board (about 35+ stones). Other full columns do nothing. Rare exception: openings made almost entirely of column-0 moves.

Mostly early-game: a bottom-row configuration where the opponent has stones at the bottom of columns 1 and 5 (often 4 too) and I have the bottom of columns 3 and 6, with no opponent stone at the bottom of 3 or 6. Opponent stones directly above theirs in row 2 (columns 1,4,5,6) suppress it; my stone on (row 2, col 3) boosts it. Firing fades as the board fills; late-game firing is only partly explained.

Early-to-middle positions with a low, centre-left cluster: my stones on the bottom of columns 3-4 and at row 2 of column 3, the opponent's stones directly on top at row 1 of columns 3/4 and flanking on the bottom row at columns 2 and 5, with cell (2,4) still empty. Any stone at (2,4), my stones on row 1 right of centre, or tall outer columns switch it off. Graded, additive; no single cell is sufficient.

Fires when the side to move has a game-winning, practically unstoppable position, mostly an immediate winning drop: strongest (top band) when the winning landing cell has another of my winning cells directly above it (typically centre column 3, row 1, in a late, crowded board), also on two simultaneous immediate wins and on lone immediate wins after move 14. Early single wins, vertical wins and losing double must-blocks are weak.

Mostly fires at exactly 6 stones (move 7): strongest when the first player's stones are in columns 0/2/4 (not 3/5), the opponent's in 2/5, and the opponent's last move was in 4 or 6. A weaker second case is the late middlegame (28-32 stones) right after the opponent plays column 0, with columns 1, 3 and 6 tall and 2 and 4 short. Threats are irrelevant.

Fires when the left edge column (column 0) holds exactly four stones and the top one (row 4 from the bottom) is the opponent's, mostly when the opponent has just played it there, or when my stones sit directly beneath it. Strongest on sparse early boards. It weakens as the board fills up and with each move since that stone was played. It is off when that stone is mine, and it does not fire for other columns.

Fires most strongly when column 1 (second from left) is tall and topped by at least two of the side-to-move's stones, with column 0 empty or nearly so; stronger the taller the stack, weaker as stones (especially opponent's) fill columns 0 and 2 and as the game gets longer, boosted when the opponent's last move was in columns 4-6. A weaker early-game route: opponent just stacked on my single column-1 stone. Covers only a minority of firing.

No clean concept found. Strongest firing is a left-centre opening shape: my two stones stacked in column 2 (bottom two cells) with the cell above empty, their stones beside them at the bottom of columns 3 and 4, and column 4 at most one stone high. An opponent stone placed directly on top of my column-2 stack switches it off. Firing positions mostly have column 4 nearly empty, but that alone does not predict firing.

Fires when column 4 (just right of centre) is full and the opponent's stone is on top, strongest when that top stone sits on my stone and was the opponent's last move; activation decays over the following few plies. Top stone mine, or col 4 at heights 3-5: no firing. Early-game variant: col 4 holds exactly two stones, theirs on top (ply <= 8). Context adds a lot of unexplained variation.

Loosely tracks an opponent stone on the centre cell of the 4th row (row 3, col 3), never mine, with opponent stones under it at (row 2, col 3) or (row 2, col 4), the cell to its left (row 3, col 2) still empty and (row 3, col 5) not theirs. Strongest when the opponent has a 2x2 block in the centre (rows 2-3, cols 3-4). Many boards with these stones stay silent; far-away stones also shift it.

Late-game signal that column 5 (second from the right) is full. It almost never fires unless column 5 is full. Given that, it gets stronger when few columns are left (strongest with one or two playable columns), when an open column is nearly empty, and when the player to move is losing by force. It is weak when column 5 still has room, even in a lost endgame.

No clean concept found; firing is diffuse. Weak tendency: fires when I must block an immediate opponent threat, strongest (top 0.1%) when the opponent just played column 3 and now threatens to win on the top cell of column 3 via a row or diagonal. Plain vertical threats in column 3, and bottom-row threats, do not fire. Many firings have no threat at all, often with column 3 full.

Fires in the opening (5-7 stones) when the opponent's last stone went in columns 0-4, strongest in centre column 3, helped by opponent stones in columns 4-5 and mine in column 0. Also fires late (37+ stones) when the last stone went in column 5 or 6. Early last moves in columns 5-6 and most mid-game positions do not fire it.

No clean concept found. Loosely: early-to-middle game positions (about 15 stones or fewer) where the opponent owns the bottom cell of column 2, the cell beside it (bottom of column 3) is not theirs, and columns 1 and 4 are still low; often with opponent twos or threes on the bottom rows. Activation depends on many stones at once (e.g. column 6 contents) and is not left-right symmetric.

Loose and distributed. Fires mostly in mid-game (ply 12-28) when the opponent owns row 4 of the centre column (cell (4,3)), the cell beside it (4,4) is empty, (3,4) is not mine and (5,3) is not theirs. Strongest when their last stone landed at (3,4). Many such boards still do not fire: the activation depends on much of the board and on move order.

Needs column 4 (second from the right) to be completely full; it almost never fires otherwise. With column 4 full it is strongest when the player to move is in trouble: the opponent has threat cells stacked in the open columns, so most of my legal moves either sit directly under an opponent winning cell or ignore a must-block. Column 4 full alone, with me safe or winning, gives only weak activation.

Column 2 (third from left) holds exactly one stone. Fires strongly when the opponent has just dropped that stone into the empty column 2, especially in the opening; it weakens as stones pile up in row 1 and above (bottom-row stones barely matter). If the single col-2 stone was played earlier it fires only weakly, mainly when it is the opponent's. Never fires when col 2 has 0 or 2+ stones.

Weak layer-0 unit. Strongest when the opponent's last move was in column 1 or column 5 and the player to move has most of their stones in columns 0 and 4 (column 0 counts most), with few stones of either side in column 5. Move order does not matter. Other last-move columns give at most weak activation. Much near-threshold firing is not explained by this.

Fires mainly in early-to-middle game positions where column 4 (right of center) holds exactly one stone, so the next stone there lands on row 1, especially when the opponent has stones beside it on the bottom row (cols 2/3/5) and columns 0 and 6 are empty. A second case is the opponent having three stacked in column 4. My own stone beside or on top of the col-4 stone switches it off. Most positions matching this still do not fire.

An opening-phase move-mix detector: fires mostly in the first ~10 moves when the moves so far are concentrated in the centre column (either side) plus my stones in column 1 and the opponent's in column 0 (especially if the opponent just played column 0). Any of my stones in column 0 strongly suppresses it; opponent stones in column 1 weaken it. Peak: 3,3,1,0 or 1,3,3,0.

Fires when the opponent has a vertical run on top of column 0 (the leftmost column) with the cell above still empty: strongly (act 4-20) for an open vertical three in column 0 (a must-block), weakly (about 1-3) for an opponent pair at rows 2-3 of column 0 with column 0 exactly four high. The same threats in other columns, my own stones, and pairs at other heights do not make it fire.

Strongest in the opening (about 6-10 stones) on the left-centre: my stone at row 2 of column 1 (on top of their stone), their stone at row 2 of column 3 (on top of mine), and an empty cell between them at row 2 of column 2, best when I also hold the bottom of column 2 and I moved first. Shifted or mirrored versions do not fire. Most weak firing near the threshold has no clear pattern.

Fires when the opponent is building the bottom-left diagonal (0,0)-(1,1)-(2,2)-(3,3) (a1-d4): they hold at least 3 of those 4 cells and I hold none, i.e. they threaten the 4th cell; also when they hold (1,1),(3,3),(4,4) with (2,2) empty. Opponent holding only (0,0)+(1,1) gives weak, inconsistent activation. Own stones on that diagonal, the mirror diagonal, or shifted diagonals do not make it fire.

No clean concept found. Weak tendency: fires more often when the opponent owns bottom-row stones on the right half (cells in columns 3-6 of row 0 hold two or more of their stones and none of mine), in early or mid game with column 6 still low; this captures only a small part of firing. Firing depends on specific stone combinations, and making a cell in row 3 playable usually switches it off.

Weak, noisy layer-0 feature over which columns each side has played in: fires when a large share of my (side-to-move) stones are in column 4 AND a large share of the opponent's stones are in column 1 (either alone does not fire). Opponent stones in column 5 (and 6), and my stones in columns 1/5/6, suppress it. Slightly favoured when I am the first player and the last move was in column 1, 2 or 4; tactics do not matter.

Mostly a move-count detector: fires late in the game when exactly 27 stones are on the board (also 25, 29, 31, 33 less often), provided columns 3-4 hold many stones and columns 0-1 few; a last move in column 4 or 6 helps, in 0, 3 or 5 hurts. Separately fires at 4 stones when the last move was column 5. Even move counts essentially never fire.

Weak, mixed unit. Strongest when the opponent has a winning cell directly above column 2's landing cell (column 2 is poisoned, typically a diagonal threat at row 4), or a vertical three in column 0, while column 1 holds at most one stone and I have no immediate win. Moderate firing is diffuse: column 1 nearly empty, the opponent's last stone on row 3, a side must-block. Central must-blocks and column-1 stacks do not make it fire.

Fires when the left half of the board (columns 0-3, including the center) is full or nearly full, with column 0 especially important, while columns 4-6 are still fairly empty. Strongest when the last move went into a left column (e.g. topping off column 0); weaker when the last move was low in column 4 or 5 or the right side is also filling up. Partly-filled left halves, or a full right half, do not fire.

No clean board concept found. The unit fires sparsely, mostly in early or middle games with all columns open, often right after the opponent plays in the centre column 3, but which positions fire depends on the exact last move and even on move order, so it behaves like a mixture or lookup. Example motif: opponent has two stacked at the bottom of column 1 while I have stones in columns 4-6.

Fires when the opponent threatens to win in column 6 (rightmost), mainly when they have three stones stacked vertically on top of column 6 with the cell above empty (strongest for a stack at rows 0-2). A non-vertical must-block in column 6 above the bottom row fires weakly. Does not fire for a bottom-row horizontal threat at column 6, stacks in other columns, or my own column-6 stack (strongly negative).

Fires when the player to move has two or more of their own stones stacked on top of column 0 (leftmost), with the cell above empty and room to reach four. Three stacked (an immediate vertical win) is far stronger. Other columns, the opponent's stack, a single stone or a stack without room do not fire; an opponent threat cell higher in column 0 suppresses it.

Loosely: an early-game cluster on the left-centre of the bottom row: column 0 and column 4 empty while columns 1, 2 and 3 each hold a stone, strongest when (0,1) is theirs and (0,2) is mine. Column 0 stacked me/them/me/them from the bottom also drives it hard. Very context-sensitive; a filled column 0 (non-alternating) or column 4 suppresses it.

Weak, distributed unit. It fires most clearly when the opponent owns the bottom two cells of column 4, the cell at row 2 of column 5 is not the opponent's, and the board is in the early middlegame (at most about 20 stones). It is stronger when columns 1-3 are low. The same pair owned by the player to move, or a pair in another column, does not fire. Many firings lack this pattern.

Weak, distributed unit. Fires most strongly when the player to move owns the centre-column cell on the third row (row 2) with column 3 at least three high, the cells to its right in column 4 (rows 2-3) still empty, and no opponent stone at (2,2), (0,1) or (0,2). Typical top boards have column 3 alternating me/them from the bottom and my stone at (1,2). Many weaker firings fit no clean pattern.

Fires when the leftmost column (column 0) is exactly three stones high with an opponent stone on top, so the next stone there lands in row 4. Strongest (often 5-9) when the opponent has just played there to make three in a row up column 0 (a must-block); mixed stacks like mine-mine-theirs fire weakly and only about half the time. Vertical threes in other columns, or column 0 at other heights, do not fire.

No clean concept found. The most enriched single pattern is column 0 (leftmost) holding only the second player's stones (one or two of them, nothing else in that column), but this covers only ~40% of firing at low precision. Activation swings strongly with the exact last move and ply parity; it does not fire when column 0 is empty or tall, and is often suppressed right after a stone is dropped into column 0.

No clean concept found. Fires mostly in the opening (about 4-14 stones) when I have no stone in column 6 and the opponent sits low in the centre-right, typically on top of my stone at (row 1, col 3) or (row 1, col 5); strongest when the opponent has a diagonal (3,3),(2,4),(1,5) aimed at the bottom-right corner. Single-stone edits switch it on/off unpredictably; it rarely fires in mid/late game.

Fires when column 1 (second from left) is full, most strongly on the move that fills it (the opponent just dropped the sixth stone there), once about 12+ stones are on the board, growing with move count. With column 1 already full it also fires late in the game (about 37+ stones), more so when column 1's top stone is the opponent's and the last move was in column 0, 2 or 6. Stacking other columns does nothing.

Weak, partial fit. Mostly fires when I (side to move) have two stones on the long down-right diagonal (4,0)-(3,1)-(2,2)-(1,3)-(0,4) with an empty cell between them and no opponent stone in that 4-cell stretch (typically my stones at (1,3) and (3,1) with column 2 low). In openings, fires when my bottom-row stones sit on both sides of an empty center column. Strongly depends on move order; many matching boards do not fire.

Fires when column 4 is empty and the opponent (who just moved) has three in a line completed at row 1 of column 4, the cell just above column 4's empty bottom, so playing column 4 hands them the win. Column-4 specific: the same trap in other columns, or higher in column 4, does not fire; once (1,4) becomes a playable must-block it turns strongly negative.

Fires when the opponent has a vertical stack of their stones on top of the centre column (col 3): strongest (top activations) when three opponent stones are stacked there, raised off the bottom row (rows 1-3 or 2-4), with the cell above empty so I must block. Two stacked at rows 2-3 fires weakly; the same stacks in other columns, my own stacks, or a full/capped column 3 mostly do not.

Fires only right after the opponent plays in column 6 (right edge), in mid-game (about ply 15-30). Strength depends on how the board is filled: strongest when column 4 holds a moderate number of stones (about 3-5, roughly a fifth of all moves; an empty or completely full column 4 kills it), column 6 is still low (few earlier stones there), and the left columns 0-2 are partly filled. Early-game column-6 moves do not fire.

Fires in the opening (mostly 4-6 stones, strongest at exactly 4) right after the opponent drops a stone in column 1 or 0 (weaker for column 5 or 3; rarely for 2, 4, 6). It is stronger when my own stones sit in columns 3 and 5 and weaker when they sit in columns 0 or 4. It fades quickly as the board fills and is near zero after about 8 stones.

Weak partial pattern: early game (ply <= 18), I moved first, no immediate win, and the bottom two rows of columns 2-3 form a checkerboard: column 2 empty or my stone capped by theirs, column 3 empty or their stone with mine on top. Odd column-2 heights, column-3 height 1, or the opposite colours switch it off. Other stones modulate it unpredictably.

Weak, mixed unit. Strongest when the mover owns the 5th cell of the centre column (row 4, col 3) while column 2 is still empty or holds at most two stones, so the cell at row 3 of column 2 is floating; it is boosted by the mover's stones at rows 1-2 of column 1 (on that same rising diagonal) and a tall column 4. Filling column 2 switches it off. Many firings, especially sparse early boards, fit no pattern.

Mostly when the second player is to move early in the game and the bottom row reads: my stone in corner a1 (helped by mine on c1, theirs on b1), their stones on f1 and g1, e1 empty. My stone on b1 or b2, any stone on e1, their stone on a2, and many stones above the bottom row weaken it. Firing with the first player to move is weak and near threshold.

No clean concept. Strongest in early games (about 5-9 stones) right after the opponent plays into column 3 (or 0/2), when the opponent's stones sit low in columns 2-3 (and 0), none of theirs in column 1, and mine are on the right edge (column 6) or column 1 rather than column 0. Every extra stone, especially in columns 4-5, dilutes it; it rarely fires late in the game. Move-order sensitive.

Diffuse, graded pattern with no crisp rule. Strongest when the opponent's last stone sits high in column 1 (rows 3-5) or column 6 (rows 2-4), column 2 and column 0 are empty or nearly empty, column 4 is tall, and the opponent has stones low in columns 5-6. Opponent stones in columns 0/2 or my stones in column 3 weaken it. No single cell or threat is enough on its own.

No clean concept; likely a mixture. Fires mostly in early-to-middle games as a weak sum of cues: my stones at the bottom of columns 2 and 4, their stones at the bottom of columns 3 and 6 (column 6 otherwise empty), and their two or three stones stacked on my pair in column 5. My stone at the bottom of column 5 suppresses it. Depends strongly on move order, not just the board.

Fires mostly when the centre column is low (1-2 stones), especially with the opponent's stone at its bottom and my stone on top of it, and the opponent's last move was not in the centre. Their stones at (1,5), (0,0), (2,2), (2,4), (3,5) add to it. It is more common in the opening (ply 4-7). It is silent once the centre has 3+ stones. Weak, scattered pattern.

Weak, mixed left-side shape detector. Fires mostly when column 0 is empty or holds one stone, column 1 holds 2-3 stones, column 3 is not at height 3-4, and the bottom-left cols 1-2 form a checker: my stones at (row1,col1) and (row2,col2), theirs at (row1,col2) and (row2,col1). Early-game variant: their stones at bottom of cols 1-2 with mine at col 4 bottom and col 3 empty. Filling column 0 switches it off.

Fires most strongly when the centre column (col 3) holds exactly 3 stones, so the next centre drop lands on row 4 (row index 3), and the column to its left (col 2) is taller, with the opponent's stone beside that landing cell. A tall left side (cols 0-2) adds to it; stones on the right side reduce it. The mirror pattern (col 4) does not work. Weaker firing near the threshold is scattered and is not explained.

Fires when the opponent has three stones stacked vertically at the top of column 0 (leftmost) with the cell above empty, so I must block there; strongest early in the game, weaker late. The same three in another column, horizontal or diagonal threats at column 0, my own three there, or an already-blocked three do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.

Early-game pattern on the lower left-centre: fires when the opponent holds the bottom cell of column 4 and column 1 is still empty (or has one stone), boosted by opponent stones at (1,3), (2,2) (sitting on my stone at (1,2)) and the bottom of column 0, plus my stone at the bottom of column 5. Opponent stone at (2,4), my stone at (1,3), stones in column 1, a must-block, or a crowded late-game board suppress it.

An end-of-game unit: fires when the board is almost full. Strongest with one empty cell left (41 stones), and with 40 stones. Earlier it fires mainly when the player to move went first (even stone count) and only one or two columns are still open. With an odd stone count before 40 it is suppressed, even if the board is nearly full. It does not care which side is winning or about threats.
